text:
A curious boy named Idris asked questions constantly. “Why is the sky blue? Where does the wind go? Why do people sleep?” His teachers found him tiring, and his classmates found him strange.

One afternoon, his teacher snapped: “Idris, a sensible person doesn’t ask so many questions. Be quiet and learn what you are told!”

The boy fell silent for a week. He became pale and unhappy. His grandmother noticed and asked what was wrong.

“Teacher says that questions are foolish,” he whispered.

His grandmother smiled gently. “Do you know why you can read, why we have light in our houses and why doctors can heal the sick?” she asked. “Every single one of those things started with somebody who was brave enough to ask a foolish question.”

She gave him a small notebook. “Write your questions here. Some you’ll answer one day, and some will lead you to other questions. Never be ashamed of being curious.”

Idris filled that notebook, then another. Years later, as a scientist, he made an important discovery about water purification. At the ceremony, he thanked his grandmother and held up his first notebook.

“The answer began with a question,” he said. “And the question began with someone who told me it was all right to ask.”

Moral: Curiosity is the engine of every discovery, so never let anyone silence your questions.

quiz.q: Idris's grandmother told him questions are foolish.
What did the grandmother give Idris?
What did Idris discover as a scientist?
___ is the engine of every discovery.
